title: Sermones. De Symbolo Sermo Ad Catechumenos
author: Augustine

passages.original: Nec amphitheatri certamina seducant aut pertrahant christianum: quo quidem tanto avidius curmur, quanto tardius exhibetur. Sed etiam ibi quid non periculosum ingeritur aspectibus, quia non cruentum? ubi, sicut ait beatissimus Cyprianus, voluntas noxia ad feras homines nullo crimine damnat (Cypr. in epist. i ad Donat.). Non ergo vos, dilectissimi, i!lud spectaculum crudele invitet intueri, novem ursis duos altercantes venatores : sed delectet videre unum nostrum Danielem orando supcrantem septem leones.
passages.english: Nor should the contests of the amphitheatre seduce or drag away a Christian: indeed people run to it all the more eagerly, the more rarely it is put on. But even there, what is not dangerous that is thrust upon the eyes, since [what is] not bloody? There, as the most blessed Cyprian says, a harmful will condemns men to the beasts for no crime (Cyprian, Letter 1, to Donatus). So, dearly beloved, do not let that cruel spectacle invite you to watch two huntsmen contending with nine bears; rather let it delight you to see our one Daniel overcoming seven lions by praying.
passages.notes: Scanning errors corrected: 'curmur' read as 'curritur' ('people run'); 'i!lud' as 'illud'; 'supcrantem' as 'superantem'. The second sentence is awkward in the Latin ('quid non periculosum... quia non cruentum?'); the sense seems to be 'what is shown there that is not dangerous, since it is all bloody?' Some editions may read 'quid non... quod non cruentum'.
